questions.question: What does colonialism mean?
options: One country taking control of another and exploiting its resources and people
Two countries trading fairly with each other
A country giving aid to poorer countries
People moving voluntarily to a new country
questions.explanation: Colonialism means one country takes control of another and exploits its resources and people, as Britain did in India and South Africa.

questions.question: When did India gain independence from Britain?
questions.explanation: India became independent in 1947, after almost two centuries of British control (direct crown rule from 1858).

questions.question: What was apartheid in South Africa?
options: A system of racial segregation and discrimination enforced by law
A type of South African English
questions.explanation: Apartheid was a legal system of racial segregation in South Africa that discriminated against the non-white majority.

questions.question: Why is English widely spoken in India and South Africa today?
options: Both countries were colonised by Britain, which left English as an important language
They chose English randomly in the 1990s
American companies introduced English in the 2000s
questions.explanation: British colonisation left English as an official and connecting language in both India and South Africa.

questions.question: Which of these is part of the legacy of colonialism?
options: Economic inequality and borders drawn without regard for ethnic groups
Equal wealth between former colonies and colonisers
The complete disappearance of the English language
The end of all cultural exchange
questions.explanation: Colonialism left economic inequality, artificial borders, loss of local languages and an ongoing debate about responsibility and reparations.
